app.title: Scholar Fetcher
app.summary: A person chooses one or more literature databases, types a search query, and sets how many records to fetch, where terms should match and whether to remove duplicates. The search pages through each source with a progress bar, then merges records of the same work across sources and keeps the most-cited records up to the requested number. A summary line and a per-source table show how many records were found, how many duplicates were removed, and whether any pages were lost. The person scans the merged table and downloads it as a spreadsheet, CSV, BibTeX or RIS file for a reference manager.

task.text: Gather a deduplicated, citable set of bibliographic records for a search query from one or more scholarly databases, with counts at every stage, and export it for screening.

data.text: Bibliographic records returned by scholarly search APIs, normalized into one row per work with title, authors, year, venue, citation count, DOI, abstract or snippet, and provenance flags, plus a fetch report per source.
data.item: a bibliographic record for one published work

stage.text: identifying records for a literature review, before screening

mechanism.text: A form sets the sources, query and limits; submitting it fetches from each source with a progress bar, deduplicates, and stores the result so the counts summary, per-source detail, results table and four export buttons all render from that one stored search. Downloading one format does not run the search again.

field.text: literature search and deduplication for systematic reviews (PRISMA identification stage)

workflow.name: gather records from several sources into one deduplicated list and export it

steps.step: set what to search for and where
steps.here: a multiselect of sources (OpenAlex by default; Google Scholar only when switched on and a key is set), a query box, the number of results, a delay between pages, title-abstract or fulltext matching, an optional contact email, and a remove-duplicates checkbox
Search checks that there is a query and a source, then pages through each source, with a progress bar showing fetched of requested
records are matched on source record id, then DOI, then normalized title with first-author surname; the best-attested copy is kept and fills its gaps from the copies that were dropped

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: a success line gives the number identified, the duplicates removed, and how many are shown out of the number requested; an expander lists each source's requested, returned and failed pages, and a warning appears for any source with lost pages

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: a full-width table of the merged records, most-cited first, with records that have no count placed after those with zero
four download buttons write Excel, CSV, BibTeX or RIS from the same stored result, with a file name made from the query plus a short hash

distinctive: Records are cut down to the requested number only after deduplication, so extra records already fetched fill the places that removed duplicates leave
Missing values are never filled in: a missing citation count stays blank with a source flag, and a DOI taken from a URL is marked as derived
Lost pages are reported per source and the result is flagged as incomplete, so a short result set is not mistaken for a complete one
The paid source is hidden unless it is switched on deliberately, so a hosted copy cannot use up the owner's quota
Exports are ready for reference managers: BibTeX is LaTeX-escaped and uses stable cite keys built from each work
